details:
VRChat assets sold on Booth should have an "Add to VRChat" option that adds the asset to your VRChat account. Add a "Link Booth Account" button in VRChat, similar to the existing Discord integration. 

That's in a nutshell, here is my full vision: 

VRChat creators already sell tons of assets on booth, there's a thriving economy there. Also, some VRChat creators sell avatars inside VRChat, which is a growing economy. 

Merge them, really! Merge them! (well, the best parts of both of them).

With the recent announcement from Pixiv regarding VRChat collaboration (see here: https://www.pixiv.co.jp/2026/09/09/120000) the door is wide-open for VRChat to work with Booth to add an option on Booth avatar pages that allows purchasing and adding the  VRChat version of the avatar directly to the user's VRChat account. This should be a *separate* version of the avatar the creator specifically creates for this functionality. This can be achieved in many ways but one jumps out at me as so simple that it's obvious:

In the VRChat SDK, an option for "Upload to Marketplace/Booth" is added. This notably *does not upload the asset to Booth*, it creates a BluePrint ID specifically for the "Marketplace" version of the avatar. Then, when a user clicks the "Add to VRChat" button on the booth webpage, then signs in with VRChat, the specific version of the avatar the creator uploaded to that Marketplace Blueprint ID is added to the user's account. 

This solves many problems:

Burden of live VRC Avatar storage - Remains on VRChat (Already is, no major infrastructure changes) 

Updates to avatars - Creator simply uploads the new version to the existing Marketplace ID (if you're feeling nice, let the users pick a version/opt-out of updates, but that's bonus)

Ownership of assets purchased on marketplace - Creators now have the option to sell the assets separately from the VRChat ready-made version. 

In a perfect world, the creator would also tag the asset type on Booth. If it's an accessory, then categorize it in VRChat as an accessory! If it's an avatar, categorize it in VRChat as an avatar! 

The "Add to VRChat" button on Booth should be a separate version of the avatar, NOT included with the traditional purchase, which directs the user to a different purchase flow from the other Booth options. The button could simply be blue rather than red to make it clear to the purchaser that they're going to get the item in VRChat. 

Allows the creator to still sell their assets on Booth as they already do.

Allows VRChat and Booth to keep their databases separate.

Allows VRChat users a convenient route to adding assets to the game. 

Regarding the SDK and how creators actually upload to this: The SDK already assigns a blueprint ID to an avatar after the creator signs in with their VRChat account. If a creator is not authorized to upload marketplace avatars, simply give them a "not authorized" message. 

Long term: Create documentation (scary, I know) for creators to comply with the marketplace requirements so you can open this up to the broader community. Also, browsing the Booth store inside the VRChat avatar menu would be amazing! Even if it is restricted to avatars that have the "Add to VRChat" button on Booth enabled. Then you can have the exact same Marketplace Blueprint ID assignment system add the avatar to the purchaser's account, in the exact same way as the Booth integration. It's very possible VRChat already has existing infrastructure for this. 

in this scenario there is no risk to VRChat, Booth, creators, or users, and tons of up-sides for all! Both companies continue to do what they're already great at! With a native integration VRChat & Booth could enable creators and users to buy assets on both platforms better than they can on literally any other creator marketplace. This continues to respect Creator's ability to sell their assets directly and get paid out through Booth's monetization system, but gives them the option for an entirely new revenue stream by allowing VRChat users to directly add the avatar to their account. 

It just makes so much sense. 

There's a huge opportunity here, I sincerely hope you consider it!
title: VRChat x Booth Marketplace Integration
